chapter_seo_title: Dao of the Bizarre Immortal Ch. 289: Trust Shatters as Blind Chen Attacks
chapter_meta_description: Blind Chen reveals he never called for backup, accusing Li Huowang of being a Zuowandao imposter. A masterclass in paranoia and folk-horror trust-breaking.
og_description: Blind Chen never called for help. Li Huowang’s identity is thrown into doubt.
twitter_description: Blind Chen’s final line changes everything about this chapter.

lore_anchors.definition: A wandering spirit entity used by Daoist practitioners for gathering ingredients or performing tasks; each summon costs three months of the user’s lifespan.
A secret sect whose name derives from a Daoist meditative concept (“Sitting in Forgetfulness”); they are liars and tricksters dedicated to spreading confusion and chaos for their own amusement.
A ritual handbell used in Daoist exorcism and summoning; its piercing ring can call spirits or repel evil entities.
A fictional sect in the novel fusing Zoroastrianism (袄) and Nestorian Christianity (景); followers practice alchemical blood-sacrifice techniques.
A small local temple made of mud housing a Bodhisattva statue; in this chapter it serves as a gathering place for the mud-devils.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Blind Chen try to kill Li Huowang?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because he never actually sent for reinforcements, so the person claiming to be Li Huowang must be a Zuowandao imposter.
A spirit entity that can be summoned using a Daoist bell; it requires a payment in the user’s lifespan.
A trickster cult that lies for pleasure, often impersonating others to sow chaos.
